basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Iratusque est Cain vehementer, et concidit vultus ejus. Unde noverat Cain respexisse'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Iratusque est Cain vehementer, et concidit vultus ejus. Unde noverat Cain respexisse Dominum ad Abel et ad munera ejus; a se autem ac suis muneribus vultum avertisse, nisi quia, sicut quidam interpretati sunt, inflammavit Dominus super Abel et sacrificium ejus, super Cain vero et sacrificium ejus non inflammavit, id est igne misso de coelis hostiam Abel suscepit, quod saepissime factum offerentibus sanctis viris legimus. Cain vero ipse sacrificium suum consumere igne debebat. Nam et hoc significare videtur Apostolus, cum ait: Fide plurimam hostiam Abel quam Cain obtulit Deo, per quam testimonium consecutus est esse justus, testimonium perhibente muneribus ejus Deo (Hebr. XI, 4). Testimonium ergo perhibuit muneribus Abel Deus per ignem, haec suscipiendo de coelis, quo etiam Apostoli testimonio docemur, quod hostia Abel per fidei illius devotionem acceptabilis Deo facta est, et e contrario subintelligere debemus Cain propterea reprobatum, quod non integra suo Conditori fide servierit.
